newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam marks birthday with mosque building.
newsitem.headline: Saddam marks birthday with mosque building.

text.p: Iraqi President Saddam Hussein has ordered that one new mosque be completed and the foundation stone for another be laid at every year's celebrations for his birthday, the official Iraqi News Agency reported on Thursday.

"The leader president has decreed that one mosque be opened and the foundation stone for another be put with every annual memory of his excellency's birthday," INA said, quoting Hussam Khadouri, head of the engineering department at the presidential office.
Saddam celebrates his 60th birthday on April 28 and Khadouri said one new mosque will be opened and work on another will start on the same day.
Khadouri said his office had so far built or renovated more than 12 mosques or holy shrines throughout the country.

Saddam intends to build a grand mosque in each of Iraq's 18 provinces, all bearing his name, and one such mosque has already been constructed in Tikrit, his birth place. Work on two others will soon start in Ramadi and Babel.
Khadouri said his engineers were about to finish designs for another grand mosque in Baghdad, on which work was expected to start in coming weeks.
